newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits fall 12.0 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits fall 12.0 pct in May.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in May fell 12.0 percent to C$2.44 billion, seasonally adjusted, from April, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
May Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month fall of 0.1 percent in May after a 9.3 percent rise in April.
Statistics Canada said the fall in May was due mainly to non residential permits which fell C$855 million to their second lowest level this year.
However, the non-residential permit level in April was exceptional, the highest in almost seven years, the federal agency said.

The overall drop was slightly offset by a rise in the value of building permits for housing. Housing permits rose 1.4 percent in May from April, up C$1.6 billion, as short-term and long-term mortgage rates declined, Stats Canada said.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction-related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
